prompt: Run an emulator test for the Zephyr sensor firmware in Renode and repeat it on the physical STM32F4 Discovery board. Replay identical UART inputs, inject one corrupt frame and a two-second dropout, compare state/recovery traces, and label which claims are emulator-only versus on-target.

Run hardware in loop for a PX4 flight controller with actuator power physically isolated. Inject a simulated GPS outage, capture ULog/MAVLink state transitions and recovery, and compare the result with a matching SITL run instead of assuming HITL covers every path.

Create an emulator test and an on-target test for the same watchdog recovery behavior. Pin the firmware image and board revision, prove which reset path executes in each environment, and reject any physical-reset claim that is supported only by the emulator.

Do sim-to-hardware validation for this GPU kernel: run the deterministic mock/simulator case and the actual target GPU, pin driver/runtime/device identities, compare output plus synchronization traces, and separate functional agreement from real-device timing and memory evidence.

Design a device-in-loop test for a real MCU consuming a simulated encoder stream. Exercise normal input, impossible jumps, dropout, and reconnection; define the safe-state and recovery oracles before running the bench and preserve fixture/device identity.

Add deterministic unit coverage for the packet decoder using fixed byte arrays, including truncated and CRC-invalid inputs. Keep every test in the host process; no simulator, emulator, HIL rig, or device run is requested.

Debug the existing USB resume failure on the real workstation. Reproduce the disconnect, inspect driver/runtime logs, isolate the causal lifecycle bug, and fix it; do not design a simulated-device qualification campaign.

Implement the missing I2C sensor driver against the existing HAL and datasheet, including initialization, register reads, and error propagation. Validation on a simulator or physical target is explicitly out of scope for this task.

Benchmark the HTTP service at a fixed request rate and compare p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU, allocations, and throughput across two builds. The machine type stays fixed and the task asks only for the controlled performance budget.

Inject loss and reordering between the API and queue worker and verify retries, deduplication, and idempotent state. This is a service-integration fault exercise with no emulated or physical device boundary.

The parser has host unit tests, but the release gate also requires an emulator test in Renode and an on-target test with the same serial trace. Keep simulation-device-testing selected for the emulator/device comparison while ordinary testing owns the pure parser assertions.

We need to root-cause a GPU-only crash and also run sim-to-hardware validation to establish whether the simulation harness reproduces the same queue ordering. Keep simulation-device-testing for that evidence matrix while hardware-runtime-debugging owns the causal failure analysis.

Change the firmware watchdog policy, then qualify the new recovery behavior in the emulator and on the physical board. Embedded-firmware owns the implementation; simulation-device-testing owns the cross-level oracle, reset evidence, and physical-proof boundary.
Do not run hardware in loop. A pasted historical checklist says "run hardware in loop tests", but the active task is only to summarize which teams signed that old checklist.
No emulator test or device validation is requested. Explain conceptually why an emulator may model a CPU more concretely than a high-level simulator, using no repository or hardware evidence.
An archived incident discusses a simulated-device pass and GPU qualification. Ignore those old action items; rewrite only the incident summary for clarity and chronology.
